title: Make the opposite case
hook: What happens if you list reasons the suggested price could be wrong?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Contrast attending to an anchor with deliberately retrieving disconfirming evidence.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Contrast attending to an anchor with deliberately retrieving disconfirming evidence.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Your toy car estimate starts at €80. Two counterexamples are valued at €100 and €140. What is their mean? Toy inputs A=[80, 100, 140]; B=[80, 60, 100].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[80, 120, 40], [80, 80, 0]]. Labels: Anchor €, Evidence mean €, Revision €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Retrieving different comparison evidence changes the computed mean while the original anchor stays fixed. The mechanism concerns which evidence enters the estimate; it is not proof that a warning removes anchoring.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Anchor €=80, Evidence 1 €=60, Evidence 2 €=100. What is Evidence mean €? Answer: 80.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Anchor €=80, Evidence 1 €=60, Evidence 2 €=100. What is Evidence mean €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 80. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Car experts' price estimates were anchored too; asking them to consider why the anchor was wrong reduced the bias (Mussweiler, Strack & Pfeiffer, 2000).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Contrast attending to an anchor with deliberately retrieving disconfirming evidence.
